tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

scope-20-offerings-verification-status: Abstract and Table 1 note: the page states its own inventory (20 offerings) and verification status (17 verified, 2 quote-only, 1 withdrawn), and Table 1 lists them consistently. It is the authors' own statement of what they cover.
pasqal-fresnel-eur-conversion: Table 1 note: the paper states how its own table value was derived (EUR 3,000/QPU-hr at 1.1622 USD/EUR on 2026-09-04). 3,000 x 1.1622 = 3,486.6, matching the $3,487 in the table.
annealer-pricing-not-comparable-to-gate-: Table 1 note: the authors state that D-Wave is included for completeness and that its pricing is not directly comparable to gate-model machines. A scope limit on their own comparison table.
reverification-cadence-and-cross-checks: Section 7: the authors state their own verification procedure (90-day re-fetch, pre-deploy gate, cross-check against the AWS Price List API publication 2026-08-31, Aria confirmed withdrawn). It is a statement of their own protocol, not a result.
researchcyc-size-1074484-assertions: Section 1, p.1: the authors state the size of the KB they translated (1,074,484 assertions, 122,658 symbols). The Section 3.6 statistics use the same total. The SUMO comparison is a cited figure, but it is not the core of the value.
folification-meaning-of-higher-order: Section 1, p.1 and Section 3, p.2: the authors define their own loose use of the term 'higher-order' in both places.
folification-untranslated-ten-percent-ma: Section 6, p.7: the authors state that the untranslated 10% may form the core of Cyc's ontology and that a large query corpus is needed to verify it. The 90% figure agrees with Section 3.6 (960,327 of 1,074,484). The value states the limit as a hypothesis, which is what the paper says.
folification-queries-measure-translated-: Section 6, p.7: the authors name the measurement (queries answerable by both ResearchCyc and an ATP system) and say experiments are still needed. They do not report the percentage. A stated limit on their own work.
folification-microtheory-ist-genlmt: Section 3.1, p.2: the paper defines the context system it translates (mt, hierarchy with inheritance from parents, ist(k, phi), genlMt). The genlMt statement is in the passage text although not in the quotes.
folification-two-fol-methods-for-context: Section 3.1, p.2: the paper defines the two FOL methods (separate modules compiled to a flat KB, as in SUMO, and an mtVisible approximation of ist). The value matches the passage.
folification-inter-context-reasoning-lim: Section 3.1, p.2-3: the authors state that both methods cannot represent inter-contextual reasoning, and they give the mtVisible(k1) => (mtVisible(k2) => phi) example, which is equivalent to the swapped form, 'not intended at all'.
folification-mt-combined-method-baseKB: Section 3.1, p.3: the authors state how their tool treats contexts (mtVisible prefix in general, none for UniversalVocabularyMt or BaseKB because they are visible to practically every query).
folification-contexts-only-approximate: Section 1, p.2: the authors state that axiom schemata translate precisely (with a size increase) and that contexts only approximately. A limit stated on their own translation.
folification-ontology-unary-predicate-pe: Section 3.2, p.3: the authors state how the FOLifier translates collections and genls (unary predicate per collection, forall x Fruit(x) => PlantPart(x)) and how reified collection-denoting terms such as (JuvenileFn Human) are handled (names concatenated).
folification-rule-macro-predicates-schem: Section 3.3, p.3: the authors state how rule macro predicates (TransitivePred, relationAllExists) and argIsa assertions are translated. 'Usually straightforward' is the authors' wording and the value keeps it.
folification-variable-arity-handling: Section 3.4, p.3: the authors state that bounded arity can be suffixed, that unbounded arity (TheSet) has no straightforward translation, and that the different predicate translates into O(n^2) inequalities. The suffix example is missing in the text layer but the value says so.
folification-exceptions-not-handled: Section 3.5, p.3-4: the authors state that exceptFor and exceptWhen give non-monotonic behavior, that the general case is more difficult, and that 'Currently, our FOLifier does not handle exceptions.'
folification-untranslated-reason-definit: Section 3.6, p.4: the authors state the reasons for untranslated assertions (Lambda and Kappa inherently non-firstorderizable; initial implementation handled only fixed-arity relations; FUNCTION ARG CONSTRAINT not handled). All three are limits of their own tool.
atp-experiment-setup-8-queries-100k-axio: Section 5, p.5-6 and footnote 2: the authors state the experimental setup (8 queries chosen before any experiment, none inherently higher-order, random subset under 10% of axioms checked by hand, VAMPIRE/SPASS/E, Athlon 2800 with 512 MB, SPASS run on OpenCyc). All details are in the passage.
atp-experiment-prover-settings-uniform-s: Section 5.1, p.7: the authors state that they did not experiment extensively with parameter settings, used a uniform Set-of-Support setting, and that E simulates SoS with clause weighting. A stated limit of the experimental setting.
atp-experiment-conditions-favor-provers: Section 5.1, p.6: the authors state the deviations in testing conditions (KB scaled below 10% for provers versus unmodified KB for Cyc, query context flattened into BaseKB for all but the last query, last query in TerrestrialFrameOfReferenceMt) and say they erred on the side of the provers. It is their own statement of their setup.
atp-experiment-alternative-explanations: Section 5.1, p.7: the authors list two explanations they did not rule out (non-ideal prover settings; incomplete FOLification omitting key axioms) and say they hypothesize the second is not the case and plan to test it.
atp-experiment-too-few-results-for-confi: Section 5, p.5 and Section 6, p.7: the authors state they could not obtain extensive results, that they present initial work and speculation, and that much work remains before a fair comparison. They also say that whole-KB experiments would allow hundreds of queries.
folification-future-work-benchmark-and-h: Section 6, p.7-8: the authors state their planned work (large query corpus, HL modules, TPTP benchmark suite discussed with the maintainers) and pose the open questions in their own words. It is a statement of what the paper has not done.
appendix-scope-55-ncfs: About This Appendix, p.iii: the appendix states it holds assessments of quantum computing vulnerabilities for each of the 55 NCFs, to help CISA prioritize assistance. The quotes are verbatim and the passage confirms them.
appendix-project-sponsor: About This Appendix, p.iii: the HSOAC project for NRMC/CISA and the disclaimer on DHS opinion or policy are stated in the document. The sponsor line in the same passage confirms it.
appendix-published-2022: Front matter, p.ii: the document states 'This research was published in 2022. Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.'
definition-confidentiality-lifetimes: NCF 43 Synopsis and NCF 13 Urgency: the paper defines, in parentheses, a long confidentiality lifetime as more than ten years and a moderate one as one to ten years. The same usage repeats across many NCFs.
method-assumption-pqc-products-available: NCF 32 footnote 2, p.NCF32-2 (repeated in other NCFs): the authors state the assumption that PQC products and services are available quickly after the NIST standardization ends, so organizations can wait until planned end of life of hardware. It is a stated assumption of their own method.
spv-measurement-scheme: Introduction, p.2: the paper describes its own technique (photon counting with a Geiger-mode APD, 50 MHz pulses, counts integrated over a dwell-time by an FPGA into a time-series).
spv-transceiver: Setup, p.2: the paper describes its own transceiver (angle-polished SMF with aspheric lens, MEMS mirror, monostatic coaxial) and says the low NA of the fiber acts as a spatial filter. It is a design statement, not a result.
spv-test-geometry: Setup, p.2: the target is a PZT at 1 m, with the beam fixed at nearly normal incidence and parallel to the axis of displacement.
spv-power-detector: Setup, p.2: 0.15 mW average outgoing power, fiber attenuators for photon-starved conditions, and an InGaAs APD with 10% efficiency in a 1 ns gate, about 50 kHz dark counts and 100 ns deadtime.
spv-laser: Setup, p.2 and Fig. 1 text: mode-locked laser with 6 ps FWHM at 50 MHz and 1554 nm; Gaussian beam diameter 2.2 mm.
spv-circulator-isolation: Setup, p.2: the fiber optics circulator separates outgoing pulses from backscattered photons with a minimum isolation ratio of 55 dB. The sentence runs across a column break but reads whole.
photon-count-model: Eq. (1), p.2-3: the paper defines the photon count as N(t) = Phi(t) eta_det dt, with the flux and efficiency terms named, and states that it holds when the detection rate is much less than 1 per gate.
cnr-definition: p.3: CNR 'is defined as' dN/sqrt(N1+N2), citing [20-22] for the form. The paper uses it as its own working definition, with dN = |N1 - N2| as signal contrast. The CNR > 1 criterion is the paper's stipulated discrimination condition, not a derived result.
sine-model: Eq. (2), p.3: the paper models the small-amplitude vibration series as N(t) = A sin(2 pi f t) + N-bar, with f the vibration frequency. This is the paper's own model, stated as the form it uses; the value claims no more.
scope-limit-test-conditions: Setup, p.2: the paper states that its tests use a PZT at 1 m with a nearly normal beam. I read the whole letter, and no other target, range or outdoor condition appears. The absence is read from the full text.

theory_low.braket-10000-shot-cost-arithmetic: Section 3 and Table 2: arithmetic ($0.30 task fee + 10,000 x per-shot price) over list prices taken from the AWS page. The numbers check ($4.55, $800.30). It is a derived figure that inherits the price risk and is not a basis for HIGH.
theory_low.braket-per-shot-spread-more-than-180x: Section 3 and Section 1: a ratio computed from cited list prices (0.08 / 0.000425 is about 188). The 175x figure in Section 1 is the same kind of computed ratio, and the cause (qubit technology) is the authors' interpretation. No basis for HIGH.
theory_low.use-case-costs-pilot-and-vqe: Section 4 and Table 3: arithmetic over list prices (for example 200 x (0.30 + 1000 x 0.08) = $16,060; 200 x 0.725 = $145). Derived figures that depend on list prices; the 200 x 1,000-shot VQE workload is an illustrative assumption.
theory_low.iqm-garnet-circuit-costs-table3: Table 3: derived cost rows from list prices (0.30 + 100 x 0.00145 is about 0.45; 0.30 + 10,000 x 0.00145 = 14.80). Arithmetic over cited prices, not a basis for HIGH.
theory_low.ibm-flex-vs-payg-breakeven-300-minutes: Section 6 and Section 8 FAQ: arithmetic over IBM list prices (400 x 72 = 28,800 = 300 x 96). It assumes the full 400-minute annual minimum is bought and inherits the price risk. A computed figure, not a basis for HIGH.
theory_low.cheapest-per-shot-rigetti-cepheus-braket: Section 8 FAQ: a comparison over the page's own list-price table, limited to shot-metered gate-model access. The $4.55 figure is arithmetic and the IBM free-tier statement is a vendor list price. Inherits price risk.
theory_low.snr-dwell-bandwidth-tradeoff: p.3: the SNR = sqrt(N) scaling for Poisson counting and the dwell-time versus bandwidth trade-off (dB = 1/2 dt, Nyquist) are standard results the paper only states. Nothing is derived or proved in the paper, and the quotes do not carry the sqrt(N) part.
theory_low.std-metric: Eq. (3) and text, p.3: the combination of the sine-wave rms and the shot noise, and the claim that sigma_m / sqrt(N-bar) scales linearly with amplitude and equals 1 for pure shot noise, are stated without derivation. The text layer also garbles Eq. (3). It is a proposed metric argued informally.
theory_low.fft-noise-concentration: p.4: the peak SNR definition (FFT amplitude at the signal frequency over the standard deviation at other frequencies) is a definition, but the value also states that white noise spreads and the signal condenses after the FFT. That is a general explanation that is not proved in the paper. A mixed value, so it is graded low; the definition alone would be HIGH.
